:::{#exr-many-vectors-dependent-practice}
#### Testing four vectors in $\reals^3$ for linear independence

A table of data with more features than observations
has more [columns](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-column) than each column has entries,
and @thm-many-vectors-dependent settles such cases without any arithmetic.
Let

$$
\vecf{v}_1 = \sbmat{1 \\ 2 \\ 3},
\quad
\vecf{v}_2 = \sbmat{4 \\ 5 \\ 6},
\quad
\vecf{v}_3 = \sbmat{7 \\ 8 \\ 10},
\quad
\vecf{v}_4 = \sbmat{1 \\ 0 \\ 1}.
$$

Are these four vectors in $\reals^3$ [linearly independent](#def-linearly-independent)?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Compare the number of vectors with $p = 3$ in @thm-many-vectors-dependent.
